title: Existence of simultaneous normalized finite-ring operations
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring. For the constant ring sheaves and their constant-section structural maps, there exists a simultaneous presentation in the sense of [def-sp-compact-projection-presentation] whose inverse open projection and inverse open base-change mates are isomorphisms. There is no hypothesis on a scheme morphism beyond being a scheme morphism; the ambient derived categories are unbounded and uncompleted.

proof.text: Use the actual constant commutative ring sheaf on each pro-etale site. Its inverse-image coefficient comparison is invertible. The module adjunction and exactness give Operation; K-injective resolutions give its right derived operation. Choose one flat-term K-flat tensor model per scheme. Transport the canonical tensor comparisons to those fixed models using their localization representative characterizations.

source.place: Proof (2), compatibility of compact-support projection with base change

proof.text: Use exact open extension by zero, transported through the unique adjoint isomorphism to actual module pullback. Its unit is invertible. The iterated fibre-product comparison defines the direct-image square and has the displayed action on sections. The normalized open theorem identifies the resulting open tensor and square mates with invertible comparisons. Adjunction and localization uniqueness preserve these properties under the preceding transports.
